venue: Family Dog at The Great Highway
supporting_acts: Commander Cody & His Lost Planet Airmen

ai_show_review.summary: Blazing Not Fade Away→Lovelight and tight Garcia leads
ai_show_review.blurb: The set builds from acoustic‑flavored numbers into a high‑energy second half highlighted by an ecstatic Not Fade Away → Turn On Your Lovelight sequence and a soaring Lovelight finale. Jerry’s guitar is on fire, Phil’s bass thumps away, and the band delivers tight renditions of Good Lovin’, China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider > High Time and Easy Wind.
ai_show_review.review: On February 27, 1970 the Grateful Dead took the Family Dog at The Great Highway into a classic early‑70s groove. From the opening “Cold Rain And Snow” through a melodic “Me And My Uncle” and a soulful “Dancin’ In The Street,” the first half set a relaxed tone that gave way to a powerful surge of rock energy. Highlights include a blistering “Easy Wind,” a tight “Good Lovin’” sandwich around the drum break, and a seamless “China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider > High Time” jam that showcases the band’s telepathic interplay. The centerpiece is the incendiary Not Fade Away → Turn On Your Lovelight transition, which erupts into an ecstatic Lovelight finale that left the audience buzzing. Jerry Garcia delivers some of his “finest stuff ever,” with soaring leads and crisp solos; Phil Lesh’s bass thumps away in a “phenomenal” fashion, laying down a solid foundation for Bob Weir’s melodic vocals on “Me And My Uncle.” Pigpen’s contributions sit comfortably in the mix, while Mickey Hart and Bill Kreutzmann keep a steady pulse throughout. The two available soundboard recordings capture the performance with crystal‑clear balance—especially the Charlie Miller transfer, which preserves every nuance of this unforgettable night.

best_recording.reason: Charlie Miller’s soundboard transfer is crisp, balanced and captures the full show (tape runs out only at the very end), making it the most complete and sonically superior source.

key_highlights: Epic Not Fade Away → Turn On Your Lovelight transition with pandemonium‑level energy
Jerry Garcia’s tight leads and soaring solos – “finest stuff ever”
Phil Lesh’s phenomenal bass thumping away, providing a rock‑solid foundation
Seamless flow from China Cat Sunflower through I Know You Rider into High Time

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia is at his finest – tight leads, soaring solos and an overall “finest stuff ever” vibe.
band_performance.Phil: Phil’s bass is phenomenal, thumping away with unbelievable harmony work that drives the band.
band_performance.Bob: Weir’s vocals on Me And My Uncle are melodic; vocal interplay with Pigpen gets special mention.
